newsitem.title: USA: Westinghouse offers buyouts to 4,600 workers.
newsitem.headline: Westinghouse offers buyouts to 4,600 workers.

text.p: Westinghouse Electric Corp offered buyout packages to about 4,600 employees in its Energy Systems business unit, a company spokesman said.

The buyouts were offered to reduce staff levels because the Energy Systems unit has struggled with weak business conditions, he said. "We have too many people, given the flat business the unit is experiencing," he said. "The workforce is larger than it needs to be."
Energy Systems employs a total of 6,600 people. About half of them reside in the Pittsburgh area.
Employees received letters late last week detailing the buyout offers, the spokesman said. Employees have until October 11 to accept.

Westinghouse is not expected to take any charges against third-quarter earnings as a result. The company is expected to announce in the fourth quarter its strategy to split its industrial and broadcast businesses.

The offer is being made to workers in some departments with 10 or more years of service. Those who accept will receive one week's salary for each of the first five years of service; 1.5 weeks' salary for each year from six to 15 years of service; and two weeks' salary for each year over 15 years of service.
Health and dental coverage would also be provided.
